key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on constituent chemistry: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide helps passivate the surface.
engineering_relevance: Controlling ink composition and precursor addition order can help preserve MXenes and tune their surface chemistry for perovskite solar-cell integration.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track chemical and surface changes.
Use density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS and DFT findings indicate rapid degradation with iodine and polyiodides, slower oxidation with PbI2, and hydrogen-bond-mediated stabilization with MAI.
watch_item: The abstract reports precursor-level chemistry, not device-performance gains; precursor addition order requires careful control.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
